name: jev-reader-state-information-v1
selection: All 46 exposed C20 dev cases, all four prefixes on the frozen CE fixed-four path; no selection by score or new target answer.

views.full: Reuse the original full-input first prediction at each prefix.
views.titles_only: Keep opened IDs and titles; omit opened text. All remaining candidates, question, criteria and order stay identical.
views.ids_only: Keep opened IDs; omit opened titles and text. All remaining candidates, question, criteria and order stay identical.

sampling: Frozen float32 CE model, eval mode, seed 0, same NativeDecision adapter and 8192/512 capacity. No new weights, QA or HTTP.
reuse: Literal-equal empty-prefix inputs reuse original first predictions; literal-equal perturbed inputs reuse their first result. No fingerprints or SHA checks.
primary: Action/top-open sensitivity and probability change on nonempty prefixes; aggregate within original source families. Empty prefixes are unchanged controls.
secondary: Acceptance against the existing source-qualified true-state annotations, same targets for all views; masked and unreviewed rows remain separate. No new labels or dev training.
interpretation_limits: Input perturbation of a model trained with full state; it is not a retrained stateless baseline or evidence of optimality.
All positions remain on the original fixed-four path; no on-policy consequences or Reader quality are inferred.
Hidden read content can make true-state targets unidentifiable. Retained target acceptance measures information loss, not valid supervision for a new hidden-state task.
Removing fields also shortens inputs and shifts positions; titles/IDs retain prefix and selection information. No length-only or total-state-removal causal claim.
Source-qualified annotations cover only seven targeted source rows, including masks, not a representative noise-rate sample.
No independent generalization, confidence calibration, learned stopping utility or whole-pipeline net benefit is established.
